notes: The supplied 'unto' before בֵּית עֲצַבֵּיהֶם answers to the verb's valency, not to a case-function of the noun: בִּשַּׂר takes its recipient as a direct object (the coordinated אֶת־הָעָם is marked, and 1CH.10.9 marks both recipients with אֵת), so rule 33's direct-object question sends the word to the verb under rule 44's supplied-preposition clause, exactly as the marker on the second recipient takes 'to' under rule 16's first family.
